context:
Goal: a grant you type in one session reaches the session it names.
Problem (risk): the probe you allowed in item 222 cannot place its hook. The frozen-path guard refused its .claude/settings.json write, and auto mode refused the Write as "[Auto-Mode Bypass]".
Based on (ruling): item 222 a set the probe's acts as a child cloud session. Asked again because those acts are refused, so the probe cannot run as you allowed it.
Based on (read): the lane's plan, section 1, line 72. The 11-06 measure by session_013NEJKzxRE91RXP3PNdpC7J ran a nested `claude -p --permission-mode auto` with scratch settings.
Departs from: item 222 a's acts (a child cloud session that writes .claude/settings.json) — the probe's first test runs in a nested headless session with scratch settings, with no repo write.
Meanwhile: only the lane's test-author runs.

options.gain: It measures the one fact still unmeasured (whether a hook can lift a refused act), and the build can start.
options.label: Run the first test headless, the 11-06 way
options.lose: It tests a headless session, not a cloud one, so a cloud difference would stay unseen.

options.label: Drop the probe and build on the 11-06 measure
options.lose: Whether a hook can lift a refused act stays unmeasured, and the build rests on that.

options.label: Park the lane
options.lose: The grant gap stays open, and the build waits.

reply: 11:56 CST Nov 8: a, routed to lane grant-reaches-lanes. The first test runs headless, the 11-06 way, with scratch settings and no repo write. The result lands in decision grant-reaches-lanes.
short: Grant probe: headless run, drop it, or park
title: Run the grant probe in a headless session, since the cloud refuses its hook write?
